new_entities.name: High serum PFAS burden
aliases: elevated serum per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances
new_entities.description: Above-background serum concentrations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances measured in human biospecimens.

edges.effect_quant: In a 4-year community cohort, branched PFOS and PFHxS predicted greater eGFR decline, and PFNA as well as branched PFOS were associated cross-sectionally with much lower eGFR and higher CKD odds. A proof-of-concept young-adult cohort also linked each standard-deviation increase in PFAS burden to 2.4% lower follow-up eGFR.
edges.population: adults and young adults with repeated serum PFAS measurements and longitudinal kidney-function follow-up
edges.mechanism: The kidney is a major target for PFAS accumulation and excretion, making chronic exposure biologically plausible as a contributor to tubular and glomerular stress. The human literature increasingly suggests a compound-specific nephrotoxicity signal rather than a uniform effect across all PFAS congeners.
edges.summary: High serum PFAS burden appears associated with worse kidney trajectories, especially when exposure is sustained and congener-specific analysis is used. The evidence is still early and somewhat heterogeneous, but the direction is increasingly consistent enough to justify kidney monitoring in highly exposed groups.
edges.caveats: Some associations differ by PFAS isomer and study population, and reverse-causation concerns remain for cross-sectional analyses because kidney handling also affects measured PFAS concentrations. This edge is best read as an emerging but plausible nephrotoxicity signal rather than as a settled causal estimate for every PFAS compound.

evidence.citation: ChenCY et al 2025 Ecotoxicol Environ Saf
evidence.notes: Perfluoroalkyl substances exposure and kidney function decline in a community-based prospective cohort.

evidence.citation: HampsonHE et al 2024 Sci Total Environ
evidence.notes: The potential mediating role of the gut microbiome and metabolites in the association between PFAS and kidney function in young adults: A proof-of-concept study.

effect_quant.comparator: each standard deviation increase in baseline PFAS burden score versus follow-up eGFR
